results.controlIntent: (a) In accordance with [Selection: a role-based access scheme; an attribute-based access scheme], establish and administer privileged user accounts; (b) Watch privileged role or attribute assignments; (c) Watch changes to roles or attributes; and (d) Take away access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from both collectors reveals systemic failures across all four sub-requirements of AC-2(7).v3:

(a) **Privileged account administration (role-based scheme):** The endpoint's execution role (`SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`) carries two wildcard policies — `s3:*` on `*` and `sagemaker:*` on `*`. This is not a properly scoped, least-privilege privileged role; it is an over-broad generic role that grants far more access than the churn-predictor workload requires. There is no evidence of attribute- or role-based scoping appropriate to this model's function.

(b) **Monitoring of privileged role/attribute assignments:** No evidence of any monitoring mechanism (e.g., AWS Config rules, IAM Access Analyzer alerts, or CloudWatch alarms) for changes to the execution role or its policies was found. The role appears static and unmonitored.

(c) **Monitoring of changes to roles/attributes:** CloudTrail shows that `data-scientist-jdoe` performed a `CreateEndpoint` action 2 hours *before* the model registry approval event (deployed at 11:00, approved at 09:00 per the note — indicating the deployment preceded approval), and an `UpdateEndpoint` hotfix with no corresponding registry entry at all. These privileged deployment actions were not gated or monitored against an approval workflow, meaning changes to the operational environment went uncontrolled.

(d) **Revocation when no longer appropriate:** There is no evidence of any access revocation events, periodic access reviews, or automated de-provisioning tied to role appropriateness. The same IAM user (`data-scientist-jdoe`) retains unchecked ability to deploy and update endpoints without oversight.

Taken together, the role is over-privileged and unscoped, privileged actions are not gated by approval workflows, there is no monitoring of role/attribute changes, and no revocation controls are in evidence. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of AWS Config rules or IAM Access Analyzer monitoring for role policy changes
No evidence of periodic access reviews or entitlement certification processes
No evidence of automated revocation or de-provisioning workflows tied to role appropriateness
No evidence of a privileged access management (PAM) tool or just-in-time access controls
CloudTrail coverage completeness (e.g., data events, management event filters) could not be verified — additional human attestation needed to confirm full audit trail integrity

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
